evidence: Reading shared + profile entries with Node showed product, defect and loop-setup all install no rules/agent. Yet skills/defect/SKILL.md:15 references agent/autonomy.md, skills/rfc/SKILL.md:11 delegates level semantics to it, and skills/loop-setup/SKILL.md:11 does likewise. test/skills.test.mjs checks references against the source repository, not the selected installation; eval/run.mjs:66 supplies agent rules by default.
problem: Supported standalone profile installations omit the authority and execution rules their skills require. Repository-local reference checks and eval defaults conceal the missing dependencies.
proposal: Make required rule assets available in each affected profile without requiring native agents or kit installation. Add a profile dependency-closure check in test/registry.test.mjs and installed-tree assertions in test/cli.test.mjs.

evidence: agents/code-simplifier.md:17 instructs 'mentally run them'; its process at line 42 asks whether the result 'would pass'. rules/agent/autonomy.md:11 requires running just check, and lines 18–19 require a fresh run and reading its exit code. eval/cases/simplifier-nesting/expect.json checks textual changes but specifies no executable gate; eval/README.md says judge is a stub.
problem: The modifying agent explicitly permits imagined verification despite the shared requirement for executed checks. Its regression case can pass without demonstrating preserved behavior.
proposal: Replace mental verification with a reference to the shared execution contract. Add a regression assertion in test/skills.test.mjs against this contradictory instruction, and make simplifier-nesting execute a behavior check on the resulting artifact.

evidence: skills/defect/SKILL.md:10–13 says diagnosis is the default and /defect without fix stops after phase 3. Its L3 row at line 23 instead promises 'diagnosis and fix in one run', while the heading at line 135 again permits fixing 'only on /defect fix'.
problem: An L3 diagnosis invocation has contradictory authorization: an agent can follow the level table and modify code, or follow the invocation contract and stop.
proposal: State explicitly that invocation selects diagnosis versus fixing and autonomy controls checkpoints within that selected operation. Add an L3 diagnosis-only eval asserting no production edits or PR creation.

evidence: bin/cli.mjs:894–897 maps multiple claims for one technology to '.' and reports that this makes the recipe cover both. docs/agent-sharing.md:42 permits several non-root modules. kit/rust/rust.just:35–41 runs cargo commands only in rust_dir; it does not enumerate the claimed modules.
problem: Two independent Rust workspaces do not become one workspace by running Cargo at the repository root. Generation can fail outright or check a root workspace that excludes one of the declared modules.
proposal: Keep routing support, but refuse automatic gate composition for multiple technology roots unless their common workspace coverage is established; report the manual composition required. Add test/cli.test.mjs coverage for two independent modules and a root workspace excluding one module.

evidence: skills/rfc/SKILL.md:159–163 orders the domain check before creating the integration branch. rules/agent/autonomy.md:112 requires the RFC already committed on rfc/<slug>; line 115 requires dropping to L3 on any failed prerequisite.
problem: On a fresh L4 launch, following the numbered procedure fails a prerequisite that the next step would establish, unnecessarily downgrading authorized orchestration.
proposal: Create the integration branch and commit its RFC before checking launch prerequisites, while keeping executor launch after successful checks. Add a fresh-launch L4 eval asserting prerequisite order and retained autonomy.

evidence: registry.json:34 tells installers that mutation runs locally and 'the CI job is the witness, not the first observation'; line 30 requires mutation before pushing and calls it Tier 3. bin/cli.mjs:298 returns entry.wire for displayed wiring instructions. rules/agent/autonomy.md:14–17 explicitly makes local mutation optional; docs/adr/0002-mutation-is-a-pr-gate.md accepts that policy.
problem: The installer prints obsolete operational instructions contradicting the accepted mutation cadence. This drift reaches consumers directly, rather than remaining an internal comment.
proposal: Align registry wiring text with optional local mutation and Tier 4 CI enforcement. Extend test/registry.test.mjs to reject the retired mandatory-pre-push and CI-witness wording in emitted wiring instructions.

evidence: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:32 labels layered sources 'not yet built', while README.md documents source installation and bin/cli.mjs:800–839 applies staged layered assets and records ownership. Architecture lines 58–59 describe unchecked Claude/Cursor replacement, contrary to bin/ownership.mjs and the README ownership contract. Its ADR index labels ADR-0010 Proposed, while docs/adr/0010-installer-refuses-unexplained-tree.md declares Accepted.
problem: The required architecture entry point directs auditors and maintainers toward an obsolete implementation and decision state.
proposal: Refresh the architecture description from the current layered-source and ownership implementation. Add a test in test/registry.test.mjs comparing explicitly stated ADR-index statuses with each record's status.

note: product: Reviewed README.md's add → init → doctor path, kit/README.md requirements, registry catalogue and installer composition. No separate finding beyond the dependency and multiple-root installation failures above; manual kit wiring is explicit and consistent with the repository's ownership model.

cost: Used .work/audit-2026-10-21/cost.md: descriptions cost ~1761 tokens; all unscoped rules ~6697, including autonomy ~2871 and decisions ~1955. The largest recurring costs carry authority boundaries. No additional cut or size ratchet justified without evidence that shorter guidance preserves those behaviors.
